name: Less debug info in dev builds (debug = false or "line-tables-only")
baseline: cargo build with the dev profile's default debug = true (full debug info)
verdict_reason: A rustc-perf run by a compiler team member found builds up to 30-40% faster, mostly on incremental rebuilds, and an independent warm-rebuild test went from 7.5 s to 1.6 s. Cargo's dev profile still defaults to full debug info in Rust 1.99, which added a separate debug profile as the first step toward changing that.
tier_reason: Measured by a Rust compiler team member on the rust-lang benchmark suite and separately by a third party with a published setup; neither publishes a full results table in the text.
claimed_speedup: Up to 30-40% faster compilation in some situations, especially incremental rebuilds (rustc-perf, with lld); warm cargo run 7.539 s with full debuginfo vs 1.611 s with debug=0 and 1.507 s with strip="debuginfo" (about 4.7x, derived from page data); cold build 107 s vs 77 s with debug=0; Rust Performance Book: up to 20-40% for dev builds
workload: rustc-perf benchmark suite with debuginfo forced off; warm cargo run after a trivial edit of a crate with heavy dependencies, plus its cold build
hardware: Intel i7-10510U laptop, 42 GB RAM (third-party test)
toolchain: lld linker (rustc-perf run); mold 2.3.3 linker (third-party test)
install: [profile.dev] debug = false, or debug = "line-tables-only" to keep line numbers in backtraces
one_liner: Turning off or trimming debug info in Cargo's dev profile cuts incremental rebuild times by up to 30-40%.
how_it_is_fast: Full DWARF debug info costs time during code generation, and the linker then copies and relocates large debug sections. Turning it off removes both costs; line-tables-only keeps file and line numbers for backtraces and most of the saving. Incremental rebuilds gain the most because linking is a larger share of their time.
use_it_when: You rarely run a debugger and debug with prints or logs
skip_it_when: You step through code in a debugger: keep full debug info
You need line numbers in backtraces: use line-tables-only rather than false
caveats: The 30-40% figure is the top of a range from one benchmark run, presented as a linked results page
The third-party test is one crate on one laptop (February 2024), with mold already in place
The standard library ships with debug info, so debug = 0 alone still links some of it
tradeoffs: No variable or type information for debuggers
With debug = false, backtraces lose line numbers
On Linux, split-debuginfo = "unpacked" is a middle ground; it is already the default on macOS (since Rust 1.53)

evidence.quote: In some situations, especially for incremental rebuilds, disabling debuginfo can make your compilation 30-40% faster!
That reduces our cargo run time to 7.539 s ± 1.691 s.
With just strip="debuginfo" our time comes down to 1.507 s ± 0.301 s.
With just debug=0 we’re slightly slower at 1.611 s ± 0.329 s
setting debug=0 also improves the cold build times (77 seconds down from 107)
consider disabling debuginfo. This can improve dev build times significantly, by as much as 20-40%.
This is a preparation for transitioning the `dev` profile away from debugging to give a saner default for faster development iterations.
macOS targets now default to `unpacked` split-debuginfo.
